slides.title: Dump in *production*. Now what?
slides.voiceover: Stop guessing why production dumped at nine. Here's the five step checklist.
slides.spoken: Stop guessing why production dumped at nine. Here's the 5 step checklist.

slides.heading: The *month-end* report dumps
lines: Users see a short dump screen.
slides.lesson: A dump = SAP stops the program on a runtime error.
slides.voiceover: Nine oh five, month end. The finance report dumps. Users see a short dump screen. Everyone asks you why. A dump means SAP stopped the program on a runtime error.
slides.spoken: 9:05, month end. The finance report dumps. Users see a short dump screen. Everyone asks you why. A dump means SAP stopped the program on a runtime error.

slides.heading: The *5-step* checklist
slides.voiceover: Step one: open ST22, and filter by date and user. Step two: read the runtime error name. Step three: read the error analysis. Step four: jump to the source line. Step five: fix it, then test again.
slides.spoken: Step one: open ST22, and filter by date and user. Step two: read the runtime error name. Step three: read the error analysis. Step four: jump to the source line. Step five: fix it, then test again.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: The *real* dump
slides.title: ZFI_MONTH_END
slides.voiceover: Here's the real one. The runtime error says division by zero. The source line is the average. The item count was zero.
slides.spoken: Here's the real one. The runtime error says division by zero. The source line is the average. The item count was 0.

slides.heading: The fix: *check first*
slides.code:
IF lv_count > 0.
  lv_avg = lv_total / lv_count.
ELSE.
  lv_avg = 0.
ENDIF.
slides.voiceover: The fix: check the count before you divide. No items? The average is zero. No more dump.
slides.spoken: The fix: check the count before you divide. No items? The average is 0. No more dump.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: *Read the dump* first
slides.body: ST22 already tells you the error, the reason and the exact source line.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: the dump already tells you everything. The error, the reason, the line. Read it before you touch the code.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: the dump already tells you everything. The error, the reason, the line. Read it before you touch the code.

A 5-step SAP ABAP short dump checklist for ST22:

4. Jump to the source line where it terminated

slides.title: Your data *vanishes* at the end?
slides.voiceover: Stop losing every row when your program ends. Last time we learned the data element. Now, database tables.
slides.spoken: Stop losing every row when your program ends. Last time we learned the data element. Now, database tables.

slides.label: WHY
slides.heading: Memory is *temporary*
slides.body: An internal table lives only while the program runs. When it ends, the rows are gone.
slides.voiceover: Why do we need tables? An internal table lives only while your program runs. When it ends, the rows are gone.
slides.spoken: Why do we need tables? An internal table lives only while your program runs. When it ends, the rows are gone.

slides.label: NEW TERM
slides.heading: *Database table* = rows that stay
slides.body: A table you define in SE11. Its rows are stored in the database, for every program and every user.
slides.voiceover: A database table is a table you define in SE11. Its rows stay in the database. Every program and every user can read them.
slides.spoken: A database table is a table you define in SE11. Its rows stay in the database. Every program and every user can read them.

slides.heading: From SE11 to the *database*
steps: SAP creates it in the database
slides.voiceover: Here's how it works. Define the fields in SE11. Activate the table. SAP creates the same table in the database. Programs then read and write its rows.
slides.spoken: Here's how it works. Define the fields in SE11. Activate the table. SAP creates the same table in the database. Programs then read and write its rows.

slides.label: EXAMPLE
slides.heading: Real rows in *SCARR*
slides.title: Table SCARR: airlines
slides.voiceover: Here's an example. The SAP demo table SCARR stores airlines. American Airlines, in US dollars. Air France, in euros. Lufthansa, in euros too.
slides.spoken: Here's an example. The SAP demo table SCARR stores airlines. American Airlines, in US dollars. Air France, in euros. Lufthansa, in euros too.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Memory vs *database*
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: an internal table forgets everything at the end. A database table keeps the data for good.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: an internal table forgets everything at the end. A database table keeps the data for good.

slides.voiceover: Why does it matter? A table field never stands alone. It points to a data element. And the data element points to a domain.
slides.spoken: Why does it matter? A table field never stands alone. It points to a data element. And the data element points to a domain.
